body:
DEFERRED IN FULL (Greg via Advisor #2239, message 3c44781c, 2026-10-28T18:31:52Z), verbatim: „…DL560 odroczyć całkowicie do chwili, gdy gated control będzie ON; nie robić setupu etapów 0–2 wcześniej.” No DL560 setup or use of any stage before gated control is ON. The checklist below is kept for that moment. Status 2026-10-29: gated control is ON for the Engram project only (since 17:51Z, canary passed); the TermAl projects stay OFF pending TermAl's settings-reset fix. Stage 0 still needs Greg's word.
Linux DL560 runner (144 cores, 256 GiB), offered by Greg on 2026-10-28 (Advisor #2232, #2234). Optional.
ROLE: a test runner only. It fetches an exact commit, runs the standard launcher, and returns evidence through the TermAl runner channel. No store, claims, evaluation authority or Git push. TermAl owns the runner software.
OPERATING COST AND THROUGHPUT — Greg direct, 2026-10-29: "mam 5 aktywnych subscrypcji. limitem sa walidacje i runy, buildy. sesje operujace to, powinny byc proste i nie zuzywac duzo".
Optimize this runner for build/test throughput and low operator-model use. Reuse the existing Git, standard launcher and completion-delivery mechanisms; this is no request for a new scheduler or runner framework.
Routine flow: receive the exact Git input and one job command, start the existing launcher once, then wait for its supported completion wake. Compilation/tests execute as ordinary processes; a model does not supervise them continuously. Return compact native run/result/count/fingerprint metadata; keep full logs in their native location and inspect only the relevant diagnostics when a real failure needs investigation.
Prefer deterministic tools for routine checks. Where a model session is necessary, use a simple bounded operator role and an economical capable model. It launches/recovers existing runs and relays results; it does not author code/tests, conduct reviews, judge acceptance, retry until green or grow evidence bundles. Existing role/model and authority rules remain.
Use host CPU/RAM/disk for independent authorized jobs, with measured resource budgets and existing per-host gate/quiet limits. Scale job concurrency from measurements, not the advertised core count. Hardware capacity is not a reason to multiply model sessions or repeat a valid check on unchanged input.
This updates the operating design only. It creates no setup/enable/restart authority, no timer, no new validation gate and no change to the DL560 deferral below.
STAGE 0, SETUP (on Greg's word, after gated control is ON):
- Linux x86_64, for example Ubuntu 24.04. A non-root user. SSH with strict host keys.
- rustup toolchain 1.99.1 with clippy and rustfmt; Node 24.14.0 (unified pin, Greg #2239); git; build-essential; pkg-config; NTP.
- At least 150 GB of disk per clone; nofile at least 16384.
- Outbound network to github, crates.io and npm.
STAGE 1, QUALIFICATION (measurement only):
- A clean detached master; run `node scripts/test-launcher.mjs full`, with the default 8 test threads.
- Return results.json, the logs, rustc -V, node -v, uname -a and nproc.
- Pass bar: all stages pass and the fingerprint matches before and after. A Linux-only failure becomes its own item.
STAGE 2, HEAVY AND STRESS JOBS (measurement only):
- The Nmax matrix, 7 fixtures in parallel from separate clones.
- Repeat-stress: 20–50 parallel copies of named filters, each in its own clone and target.
STAGE 3, LATER: a landing-gate host. This needs a rule change concurred by both coordinators, with the wording sent to Greg.
